Subject: Capacity provisioning & warmup cadence for Brightfold pilot

Team —

Brightfold is kicking off a limited pilot next week (starts 2026-06-02) and they just sent the attached traffic forecast. We need a quick cross-functional alignment so we can:

- Provision a temporary quota uplift for the pilot window (expected 5 days)
- Define warmup cadence (prefix caching & KV prefill timing)
- Confirm routing and fallback policy (hosted -> dedicated fallback)

High-level numbers from Brightfold (full sheet attached): expected peak concurrent requests ~175 TPS, average tokens per request ~420, peak day token volume ~3.6M. They expect 3x baseline on day 1 and an open top-up for the following 3 days.

Asks:
- Product: any model/accuracy trade-offs we should accept? quantization profile?
- Ops (Marissa/Connor): what lead time do you need to carve provisional capacity and set routing?
- Infra (Karthik): any constraints on KV cache prefill or sequence length that would change our warmup plan?

I've attached Brightfold_warmup_forecast_v1.xlsx. Can we huddle async here and lock down a plan by EOD? Brightfold wants confirmation by tomorrow morning.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
AM, Customer Success (Launch & Scale)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity provisioning & warmup cadence for Brightfold pilot

Thanks Naomi — quick technical notes from inference side:

- Model: they intend to use Redwood-2-13B by default for latency parity. If they can accept a distilled 6B variant for lower cost, we can reduce peak GPU footprints.
- Seq length: typical 512 tokens (prompt+response) but distribution shows a heavy tail to 2k on ~8% of calls — that matters for KV sizing.
- Tokenization: a high variance in token-per-request suggests prefix caching will help but prefill should be targeted to the top 10 prompt prefixes; full KV prefill of 2k sequences is expensive.
- Quantization: recommend fp16 for quality, int4 for non-critical flows — if Brightfold agrees to the distilled model we push int4 + smaller warmup.

Warmup suggestion:
- T-48h: dry-run synthetic ramp at 25% of projected peak for 2 hours to prime kernels and networking.
- T-6h: prefix cache prefill on top 10 prefixes + 20% sample KV warmup for 1 hour.
- T-0: two staged traffic gates (50% then 100%) across 30-minute windows.

If ops needs a different cadence to match autoscaler hooks, say so and we can sync. I can produce a short playbook for the prefill script.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity provisioning & warmup cadence for Brightfold pilot

Naomi — ops constraints and what we can do:

- Lead time: For a provisional uplift in Dedicated we need at least 36 hours to resize GPU pools and update routing (shorter in emergency but carries risk).
- Allocation: We can provision a temporary 1.8x capacity uplift scoped to a named pool. We will limit the uplift window to a 120-hour max and require traffic gating.
- Autoscaler: will respect warmup cadence but we need explicit ingress TPS numbers and approximate token-per-second to set burst policies.
- Fallback: policy will fall back to hosted variants with 5s latency SLO — we need customer OK on degraded latency.

I'll attach a provisional-allocation-note.pdf with the exact ops play (allocation id placeholder).

Quick ask to Brightfold: can you provide the expected start time (UTC) and the 4-hour rolling peak TPS for the first 48 hours? That helps with prefill window sizing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood Dedicated

Attachment: provisional-allocation-note.pdf (doc stub)

Alex / Jill —

Thanks for the forecast. Internal quick plan below; we need your confirmation on two items so we can finalize ops provisioning:

1) Model trade-off: Would Brightfold accept a 6B distilled model for cost-limited flows (non-critical paths)? If yes, we'll route lower-confidence flows to the distilled variant during peak windows.
2) Start window: please confirm the UTC start for 2026-06-02 (we proposed 16:00 UTC start).

Planned rundown (subject to your OK):
- T-48h: synthetic ramp (internal)
- T-6h: prefix prefill and KV sample prefill
- T-0: staged ingress gate (50% -> 100% over 30 minutes)
- Provision: temporary Dedicated uplift (1.8x) for 120 hours; fallback to hosted with a 5s latency SLO

If you confirm model and start time, Marissa will submit the provisioning request and we will schedule the warmup script.

Best —
Naomi
